decision: New project for the comparison reel; layout = stacked split-screen (RS top, GT3 bottom, 1080x960 each) with frame-identical cuts (tools/assemble_split.py)
why: User asked for a version that splits off and shows the GT3 side-by-side; cars are landscape subjects, so two stacked 9:8 panels show both large in a 9:16 reel, and the RS panel can reuse the centre band of its 9:16 renders

decision: GT3 order mirrors the RS panel: whole | front (RS nose aero / GT3 frunk opens) | front wheel (RS fender vent off / GT3 FR wheel off, brake) | wing (GT3 wing lifts) | rear (RS diffuser, then side skirt / GT3 bumper, diffuser, lip, tail lights, engine-lid spoiler off, push into the exhaust) | breakdown (RS wheel house / GT3 skirt off along the sill to the open wheel well) | RS underbody / GT3 everything-off wide | both reassemble and lock on b74
why: Matched sections make the comparison readable; the GT3's rear has the most removed-state data so it gets the longest scene; both locks land on the same kick

decision: GT3 parts stay off until the final shot; exits follow the direction search (bumper back+down then up clear of the exhaust view, diffuser/lip back+down, tail lights and spoiler up, skirt down then out, wheel along its axle)
why: RS rule from the reviewer: parts must not clip into the car; clipcheck shows only 1-3 % of points near their own mounts at the seat instant

decision: Same music and grid as the RS v5 reel (Alkitran from 171.651 s)
why: The comparison splits off from that reel; cuts and the breakdown/kick-return moments carry over

decision: RS panel = centre band of the 9:16 v6 renders (per-shot crop_y); the tall underbody shot is rotated 90 deg to run across the panel
why: No RS re-render needed for the split; a 960-high band of the vertical underbody shot showed only the mid floor

decision: Labels: car name left + current section right in a 96 px header bar per panel (drawtext), not ScanHUD
why: Two panels need four text items; a header bar keeps every label off the scans and readable on close-ups that fill the panel
Luma clean on all 8 GT3 shots, clipcheck only seat-instant contacts, 8/8 cuts within +-0.51 frame of a kick

decision: v2: double CTA during the final reassembly scene (b62 -> fade): 'GT3 RS SCAN DATA · ILLUMAESTHETIC.COM' under the top header, 'GT3 SCAN DATA · ILLUMAESTHETIC.COM' under the bottom header
why: User: 'add a double CTA on the top and bottom frames - scan data on site'. Both scans are listed on illumaesthetic.com (Porsche 911 GT3 RS (992) 3D Scan; Porsche 911 GT3 (992.1) 3D Scan) - checked via the site's search; no prices on screen

decision: GT3 rear base rebuilt as comp_gt3b: comp_gt3 + new geometry of GT3-992-ExhaustOn-UWT (ICP-registered, 53% of points within 8 mm), g_rear restaged (parts leave half a beat faster, camera pushes in low under the lifted bumper and holds b40-44)
why: User: when the GT3 rear bumper comes off, show the bumper-removed scan underneath. No file in the GT3 Drive folder is a dedicated rear bumper-off capture (Nikitas 'Bumper Off' is the FRONT bumper; the Exhaust scans are from below), so the reveal uses every real capture of that area and frames it as the subject

decision: Ending replaced: text CTA + logo card removed; after the lock (b74) both cars sweep round the tail and land on their product listing's scan-view angle (b77), dissolve b77-b78 into a split WebZoomSplit end card (screenshots of the two real listing pages, zoom-out b78-b82, title, logo, URL), end b90
why: User: CTA must be like the 240SX videos - a screenshot of the actual website with the final shot a 1:1 transition into the website imagery. Both listings open on the same rear-right 360-viewer frame, so one matched angle works for both panels

decision: End poses from tools/silgrid.py (az/el/focal grid, distance+target fitted to the mask bbox, IoU 0.977 GT3 / 0.962 RS); silsolve's random global search stuck at IoU 0.85 with a wrong short focal
why: The listing view is ~10 m away at 30-40 mm; the local search around a 6 m guess could not reach it. Overlay checked by eye (match_end.jpg)

decision: 60 fps export: same 15 fps Blender renders motion-interpolated to 60 (assemble_split out_fps), website end card rendered natively at 60
why: User asked for 60 FPS; a true 60 fps re-render of every Blender shot is ~4x the render time, so the fast version is interpolation - in-between frames smear on the fast tail sweep
